scenes.name: Fiction

scenes.name: Wonders
scenes.desc: Student-style wonder bubbles float in. STOP 3 (share and capture).

scenes.name: Sort
scenes.desc: Bubbles sort into six buckets: How fast? Where? When? How big? What’s it made of? Can we stop it? These questions organize the year.

scenes.name: Units
scenes.desc: Seven unit cards appear; Unit 1 lights up. Each unit answers one piece.

scenes.name: Anchor

lessons.title: How Do We Talk About Motion
lessons.file: Day 2 - How Do We Talk About Motion - In Class.dc.html
lessons.guide: Day 2 - How Do We Talk About Motion - Teacher Guide.md

scenes.name: Title
scenes.desc: Day 2 · Setting up the question: How do we talk about motion? Target K1.

scenes.name: WarmUp
scenes.desc: A student walks door → desk → door. STOP 1 (warm-up).

scenes.name: Define
scenes.desc: “Twice the distance” and “zero”: both right. Distance (scalar, total path) vs displacement (vector, change in position); five vocabulary cards. STOP 2 (track problems).

scenes.name: Track
scenes.desc: 400 m track: runner laps with live distance and displacement. 1 lap: 400 m / 0. 1.5 laps: 600 m / ≈ 112 m across the field. STOP 3 (walk activity).

scenes.name: Walk
scenes.desc: Top-down grid: 5 N, 3 E, 5 S. Distance 13 steps, displacement 3 steps east. STOP 4 (discuss).

scenes.name: Asteroid
scenes.desc: Simplified map: Earth and 2026-XJ’s current position; a 1,000,000 km circle of possible moves. STOP 5 (discuss).

scenes.name: Wrap
scenes.desc: Answers: closer, farther, about the same. Then: direction matters, so we need vectors; next week motion vocabulary and graphs. STOP 6 (exit ticket).

scenes.name: Hold
scenes.desc: Hold on the exit ticket.

lessons.title: Velocity
lessons.file: Day 3 - Velocity - In Class.dc.html
lessons.guide: Day 3 - Velocity - Teacher Guide.md

scenes.name: Title
scenes.desc: Day 3 · Building the tools: Velocity, motion with direction. Target S1.

scenes.name: Recap
scenes.desc: Recap: a walker goes 4 m forward, 1 m back on a number line. STOP 1 (quick check).

scenes.name: Question
scenes.desc: Answers: distance 5 m, displacement +3 m. Then Fitchburg → Worcester: car A arrives in 1 h, car B in 2 h. STOP 2 (today’s question).

scenes.name: Define
scenes.desc: Speed = distance/time (scalar); velocity = displacement/time (vector). Car A arrow twice car B. Unit m/s. STOP 3 (convert 72 km/h).

scenes.name: Convert
scenes.desc: 72 km/h → 20 m/s with units cancelling; ÷3.6 shortcut. STOP 4 (2026-XJ in km/h and mph).

scenes.name: Asteroid
scenes.desc: 8,500 m/s ≈ 30,600 km/h ≈ 19,000 mph; bars: car, jet, 2026-XJ; about 35× a jet.

scenes.name: Match
scenes.desc: Investigation 1.1: detector, walker, target graphs: constant velocity, then a direction change. Predict, attempt, observe, refine. STOP 5.

scenes.name: Slope
scenes.desc: Three graphs: steep = fast, shallow = slow, flat = not moving; slope = Δx/Δt = velocity; flat misconception. STOP 6.

scenes.name: Sign
scenes.desc: Walker moves toward the sensor: negative slope, negative velocity. STOP 7 (what if the axis flips?).

scenes.name: Connect
scenes.desc: Answer to STOP 7: the axis flips, same walk, positive velocity. Then 2026-XJ distance vs time (illustrative): tangent slope ≈ −8,500 m/s = velocity at that point. STOP 8 (exit ticket).

scenes.name: Hold
scenes.desc: Hold on the exit ticket.

lessons.title: Velocity-Time Graphs and Vectors
lessons.file: Day 4 - Velocity-Time Graphs and Vectors - In Class.dc.html
lessons.guide: Day 4 - Velocity-Time Graphs and Vectors - Teacher Guide.md

scenes.name: Title
scenes.desc: Day 4 · Building the tools: Velocity–time graphs and vector thinking. Target R2.

scenes.name: Recap
scenes.desc: Position–time graph with a slope triangle: v = 1.0 m / 2.0 s = 0.5 m/s. STOP 1 (today’s question).

scenes.name: VT
scenes.desc: Same motion on a v–t graph: a horizontal line at 0.5 m/s. STOP 2 (sketch v–t for yesterday’s graphs).

scenes.name: Insights
scenes.desc: Five x–t → v–t pairs: steep, shallow, flat, toward the sensor, speeding up. Horizontal vs tilted; slope = acceleration preview. STOP 3.

scenes.name: Vectors
scenes.desc: An arrow: length = magnitude, direction = direction; a half-length arrow; compass. STOP 4 (draw three vectors).

scenes.name: Practice
scenes.desc: Answers on one scale (1 square = 25 mph): car, plane, runner (5 m/s ≈ 11 mph); mixed units warning.

scenes.name: Decompose
scenes.desc: 2026-XJ: 8,500 m/s at 15° toward Earth, split into ≈ 8,210 m/s toward Earth and ≈ 2,200 m/s perpendicular; tip to tail; trig box. STOP 5.

scenes.name: SixMonths
scenes.desc: distance = rate × time; 6 months ≈ 1.6 × 10⁷ s; the two rates. STOP 6.

scenes.name: Connect
scenes.desc: Answers: ≈ 1.3 × 10⁸ km and ≈ 3.5 × 10⁷ km. Then the asteroid moves with its two component shadows; NASA tracks both. STOP 7 (exit ticket).

scenes.name: Hold
scenes.desc: Hold on the exit ticket.

lessons.title: Predicting the Position
lessons.file: Day 5 - Predicting the Position - In Class.dc.html
lessons.guide: Day 5 - Predicting the Position - Teacher Guide.md

scenes.name: Title
scenes.desc: Mission 2026-XJ · In class: Where will it be in six months? Key hints for the teacher.

scenes.name: Recap
scenes.desc: v = Δx/Δt → Δx = vΔt; asteroid moves at constant speed with equal Δx each second. STOP 1 (warm-up).

scenes.name: Setup
scenes.desc: Plane with Earth at the origin; asteroid at (1.2 × 10⁸ km, 0) with vₓ and v_y arrows. Pan to the Given panel. STOP 2 (prep check).

scenes.name: Units
scenes.desc: Convert to km/s; interpret 1.6 × 10⁷ s; km vs m warning. STOP 3 (calculate).

scenes.name: Solve
scenes.desc: Δx, Δy, new x and y in the panel; pan to the plane: asteroid travels, legs, predicted point, d ≈ 3.70 × 10⁷ km; not an orbit. STOP 4 (discuss).

scenes.name: HowSure
scenes.desc: How sure are we? ±50,000 km position, ±200 m/s velocity. STOP 5 (calculate the window).

scenes.name: Window
scenes.desc: Zoomed view: position uncertainty smaller than the dot; window grows over 6 months to ±3.25 × 10⁶ km; ranges. STOP 6 (discuss).

scenes.name: Reality
scenes.desc: Straight-line model vs bending paths under the Sun’s gravity; the real window is bigger. STOP 7 (discuss).

scenes.name: Reflect
scenes.desc: Fictional scenario, real methods; better model + more observations; Days 21–22 transfer. STOP 8 (exit ticket).

scenes.name: Hold
scenes.desc: Hold on the exit ticket.

lessons.title: Vector Addition and Decomposition
lessons.file: Day 6 - Vector Addition and Decomposition - In Class.dc.html
lessons.guide: Day 6 - Vector Addition and Decomposition - Teacher Guide.md

scenes.name: Title
scenes.desc: Day 6 · Building the tools: Vector addition and decomposition. Target S2.

scenes.name: Recap
scenes.desc: Yesterday’s split: 8,500 m/s → 8,210 toward Earth + 2,200 perpendicular. Today: practice it as a tool.

scenes.name: TipTail
scenes.desc: Grid: A = 3 east, B = 4 north slides tip to tail; R ≈ 5 units at 53° N of E; √(3² + 4²) = 5. STOP 1.

scenes.name: AsteroidAdd
scenes.desc: 2026-XJ components tip to tail. STOP 2 (find the resultant).

scenes.name: Recipe
scenes.desc: Answer: R ≈ 8,500 m/s at 15°. Then the Vector Recipe Card: adjacent = V cos θ, opposite = V sin θ; worked 10 m/s at 30°; mix-up alert. STOP 3.

scenes.name: Trap
scenes.desc: Same vector with the angle measured from the vertical; components marked “?”. STOP 4.

scenes.name: Quiz
scenes.desc: Answer: vertical is adjacent → cos. Then the mini-quiz card and self-check list. STOP 5.

scenes.name: Exit
scenes.desc: A vector with its magnitude and components marked “?”. STOP 6 (exit ticket).

scenes.name: Hold

lessons.title: Acceleration
lessons.file: Day 7 - Acceleration - In Class.dc.html
lessons.guide: Day 7 - Acceleration - Teacher Guide.md

scenes.name: Title
scenes.desc: Day 7 · Building the tools: Acceleration, when velocity changes. Target R4.

scenes.name: Warmup
scenes.desc: A car accelerates from 0 to 60 mph in 6 s along a road. STOP 1 (predict its acceleration).

scenes.name: Define
scenes.desc: Answer: +10 mph each second. a = Δv/Δt, units m/s². 60 mph ≈ 27 m/s → 4.5 m/s²; bars compare with g = 9.8 m/s². STOP 2 (is braking accelerating?).

scenes.name: Direction
scenes.desc: Answer: yes. Speeding up: a with v. Slowing down: a opposite v, negative if forward is +.

scenes.name: Graphs
scenes.desc: Three v–t graphs A (rising), B (flat), C (falling). STOP 3 (identify each).

scenes.name: Slope
scenes.desc: Answers. Slope of v–t = acceleration: 12 m/s ÷ 4 s = +3 m/s²; −20 m/s ÷ 5 s = −4 m/s². STOP 4 (practice graphs).

scenes.name: Equations
scenes.desc: Reference card: v = v₀ + at, x = x₀ + v₀t + ½at². Worked: the car reaches 27 m/s in 81 m. STOP 5 (cart problem).

scenes.name: Asteroid
scenes.desc: STOP 5 answer, then Earth’s pull on 2026-XJ: g = GM/r² ≈ 2.8 × 10⁻⁸ m/s²; Δv ≈ 0.4 m/s in 6 months. Asteroid moves closer: inverse-square. STOP 6.

scenes.name: Exit
scenes.desc: A car slows 30 → 0 m/s in 5 s; blank v–t axes. STOP 7 (exit ticket).

scenes.name: Hold
scenes.desc: Hold on the exit ticket.

lessons.title: Constant Acceleration Problem-Solving
lessons.file: Day 8 - Constant Acceleration Problem-Solving - In Class.dc.html
lessons.guide: Day 8 - Constant Acceleration Problem-Solving - Teacher Guide.md

scenes.name: Title
scenes.desc: Day 8 · Building the tools: Constant acceleration problem-solving. Target R5.

scenes.name: Recap
scenes.desc: Skateboarder speeds up from 2 to 5 m/s over 2 s. STOP 1 (acceleration?).

scenes.name: Three
scenes.desc: Answer: 1.5 m/s². The three equations, each with its missing variable struck out (no Δx, no v, no t). STOP 2 (no time given: which equation?).

scenes.name: Strategy
scenes.desc: Answer: v² = v₀² + 2aΔx. Strategy: given, asked, missing variable. Example 1: car brakes 30 → 0 at −6 m/s² → 75 m.

scenes.name: Ball
scenes.desc: Example 2: ball thrown up at 15 m/s; hidden given v = 0 at the top → 11.5 m. STOP 3 (bullet train).

scenes.name: Train
scenes.desc: Answer: no Δx → v = v₀ + at → t = 160 s. STOP 4 (problem set in pairs).

scenes.name: Share
scenes.desc: How do I choose? Given · Asked · Connect; missing t / Δx / v → which equation; constant acceleration only. STOP 5 (share-out).

scenes.name: Exit
scenes.desc: Cart at +12 m/s stops at −3.0 m/s²; givens with no time. STOP 6 (exit ticket).

scenes.name: Hold
scenes.desc: Hold on the exit ticket.

lessons.title: Newtons 1st Law - Inertia
lessons.file: Day 9 - Newtons 1st Law - Inertia - In Class.dc.html
lessons.guide: Day 9 - Newtons 1st Law - Inertia - Teacher Guide.md

scenes.name: Title
scenes.desc: Day 9 · Building the tools: Newton’s 1st Law, inertia. Target R6.

scenes.name: Hook
scenes.desc: Puck slides far on ice; brick stops fast on the floor. STOP 1 (why?).

scenes.name: History
scenes.desc: Answer: friction. Aristotle (≈350 BCE): things come to rest. Galileo’s ramps: flatten the far ramp and the ball keeps going. Newton’s 1st Law card. STOP 2 (own words; net force).

scenes.name: Inertia
scenes.desc: Inertia = resistance to change in motion. Same push on light and heavy carts: more mass, more inertia.

scenes.name: Cloth
scenes.desc: Demo 1 setup: cups on a tablecloth. STOP 3 (predict).

scenes.name: Coin
scenes.desc: Answer: cloth whips out, cups stay. Demo 2 setup: coin on a card over a glass. STOP 4 (predict).

scenes.name: Car
scenes.desc: Answer: card flies, coin drops in. A car stops suddenly; the passenger lurches forward. STOP 5 (why?).

scenes.name: Asteroid
scenes.desc: Answer: inertia, seatbelt supplies the force. 2026-XJ coasts at constant velocity in space; gravity (mostly the Sun) is what pulls. To change its path, a force.

scenes.name: Exit
scenes.desc: A spacecraft approaches the asteroid; F = ?. STOP 6 (exit ticket).

scenes.name: Hold
scenes.desc: Hold on the exit ticket.

lessons.title: Forces
lessons.file: Day 10 - Forces - In Class.dc.html
lessons.guide: Day 10 - Forces - Teacher Guide.md

scenes.name: Title
scenes.desc: Day 10 · Building the tools: Forces, what pushes and pulls. Target K2.

scenes.name: Recap
scenes.desc: Newton’s 1st Law recap: a puck coasts at constant velocity until a force bends its path. “Today: what IS a force?” STOP 1.

scenes.name: Define
scenes.desc: A force is a push or a pull, measured in newtons. 1 N ≈ weight of a small apple. Forces are vectors: 2 N and 5 N arrows; same 5 N rotated is a different force.

scenes.name: Sensor
scenes.desc: Demo: Go Direct force sensor with a hook and a blank reading. STOP 2 (predict pull vs push).

scenes.name: Types
scenes.desc: Answer: pull reads +, push reads −. Five force cards: gravity, normal, friction, tension, applied.

scenes.name: Book
scenes.desc: Scenario 1: a book resting on a desk. STOP 3 (draw every force).

scenes.name: Scenarios
scenes.desc: Answer: book gravity down, normal up. Car on a road: gravity, normal, applied (engine), friction + drag. Person on a rope: gravity, tension. Not forces: momentum, speed, inertia. STOP 4.

scenes.name: Asteroid
scenes.desc: Forces on 2026-XJ: solar gravity dominant, Earth’s gravity tiny but growing, other planets negligible, friction zero, solar radiation pressure tiny. STOP 5 (which can humans add?).

scenes.name: Human
scenes.desc: Answer: add an applied force. Kinetic impactor (DART, 2022) and a nuclear blast push.

scenes.name: Exit
scenes.desc: A car coasting down a hill. STOP 6 (exit ticket).

scenes.name: Hold
scenes.desc: Hold on the exit ticket.

lessons.title: Newtons 2nd Law - Vary Mass
lessons.file: Day 11 - Newtons 2nd Law - Vary Mass - In Class.dc.html
lessons.guide: Day 11 - Newtons 2nd Law - Vary Mass - Teacher Guide.md

scenes.name: Title
scenes.desc: Day 11 · Building the tools: Newton’s 2nd Law, vary the mass. Target S3.

scenes.name: Recap
scenes.desc: A net force changes motion: a cart pushed by F. But how MUCH? STOP 1 (predict).

scenes.name: Setup
scenes.desc: Investigation 1.2: track, motion detector, cart with mass bars, string over a pulley to a hanging mass. STOP 2 (variables).

scenes.name: Run
scenes.desc: Answer: change m, measure a, keep the hanging mass constant. One trial (0.50 kg): v–t line drawn live, slope a ≈ 0.37 m/s². STOP 3 (run the lab).

scenes.name: Data
scenes.desc: Example class data: four masses, a falls from 0.374 to 0.155 m/s²; a vs m plotted with a dashed curve. STOP 4 (describe the trend).

scenes.name: Linear
scenes.desc: More mass, less a, but a curve. Doubling m halves a. 1/m column; a vs 1/m is a straight line through 0. m·a ≈ 0.19 N every trial.

scenes.name: Connect
scenes.desc: a ∝ 1/m → a = F/m → F = ma. F ≈ 0.19 N, close to the hanger’s weight 0.196 N.

scenes.name: Asteroid
scenes.desc: 2026-XJ: m ≈ 3.5 × 10¹¹ kg. F = 1,000 N gives a ≈ 2.9 × 10⁻⁹ m/s²; over 10 years Δv ≈ 0.9 m/s. Huge force short time vs small force long time. STOP 5.

scenes.name: Exit
scenes.desc: Same F on m and on 2m. STOP 6 (exit ticket).

scenes.name: Hold
scenes.desc: Hold on the exit ticket.

lessons.title: Newtons 2nd Law - Vary Force
lessons.file: Day 12 - Newtons 2nd Law - Vary Force - In Class.dc.html
lessons.guide: Day 12 - Newtons 2nd Law - Vary Force - Teacher Guide.md

scenes.name: Title
scenes.desc: Day 12 · Building the tools: Newton’s 2nd Law, vary the force. Target S4.

scenes.name: Recap
scenes.desc: Day 11: a ∝ 1/m at constant F. Today keep m, change F. STOP 1.

scenes.name: Setup
scenes.desc: Investigation 1.3: same cart, no bars; hanging mass grows 10 → 50 g. STOP 2 (predict a vs F).

scenes.name: Run
scenes.desc: F ≈ m·g: 50 g → 0.49 N. One trial with the 0.50 kg cart: v–t line, slope a ≈ 0.89 m/s². STOP 3 (lab).

scenes.name: Data
scenes.desc: Example data: five hanging masses, F and a; a vs F points. STOP 4 (shape? double F?).

scenes.name: Linear
scenes.desc: Straight line through the origin. Double F → about double a: a ∝ F. Slope ≈ 1.8 /kg; 1/slope ≈ 0.55 kg = cart + hanger; slope = 1/m.

scenes.name: Combine
scenes.desc: Day 11 a ∝ 1/m + Day 12 a ∝ F → a ∝ F/m → F = ma. Found from your own data.

scenes.name: Asteroid
scenes.desc: 2026-XJ: 1,000 N → 2.9 × 10⁻⁹ m/s²; 2,000 N → 5.7 × 10⁻⁹ m/s². Double the push, double Δv. STOP 5.

scenes.name: Exit
scenes.desc: Same m, F vs 2F. STOP 6 (exit ticket).

scenes.name: Hold
scenes.desc: Hold on the exit ticket.

lessons.title: F equals ma in Practice
lessons.file: Day 13 - F equals ma in Practice - In Class.dc.html
lessons.guide: Day 13 - F equals ma in Practice - Teacher Guide.md

scenes.name: Title
scenes.desc: Day 13 · Building the tools: F = ma in practice, net force first. Target R7.

scenes.name: Recap
scenes.desc: F = ma found from data. A 5 kg box pushed with 10 N. STOP 1 (quick check).

scenes.name: Net
scenes.desc: STOP 1 answer: 2 m/s². Net force = sum of all forces with direction. Box: 20 N applied, 5 N friction → 15 N net, a = 3 m/s². STOP 2 (4 kg, 30 N, 6 N).

scenes.name: Types
scenes.desc: STOP 2 answer: 24 N, 6 m/s². Three problem types; worked reverse problem (60 kg × 2.5 = 150 N); four-step strategy. STOP 3 (problem set).

scenes.name: Car
scenes.desc: Application: 1500 kg car slows 30 → 0 m/s in 5 s; animated braking. STOP 4 (solve it).

scenes.name: Friction
scenes.desc: STOP 4 answer: a = −6 m/s², F = −9000 N (backward). Three cars: speeding up (engine > friction), coasting (only friction), braking. STOP 5.

scenes.name: Exit
scenes.desc: STOP 5 answer: equal, net force 0. Exit ticket: 2 kg cart, 12 N push, 4 N friction. STOP 6.

scenes.name: Hold
scenes.desc: Hold on the exit ticket.

lessons.title: Newtons 3rd Law
lessons.file: Day 14 - Newtons 3rd Law - In Class.dc.html
lessons.guide: Day 14 - Newtons 3rd Law - Teacher Guide.md

scenes.name: Title
scenes.desc: Day 14 · Building the tools: Newton’s 3rd Law, action and reaction. Target R8.

scenes.name: Riddle
scenes.desc: Horse pulls cart; cart pulls back equally. How does the cart move? STOP 1 (argue).

scenes.name: Law
scenes.desc: 3rd Law: A on B and B on A, equal and opposite, every instant. STOP 2 (why don’t they cancel?).

scenes.name: Resolve
scenes.desc: Answer: they act on different objects. Forces on the cart (horse pull > friction) and on the horse (ground push > cart pull); both move off.

scenes.name: Tug
scenes.desc: Investigation 1.4: two linked force sensors read equal and opposite as pulls vary. STOP 3 (lab).

scenes.name: Results
scenes.desc: Sensor A and B traces mirror each other through jerky pulls. STOP 4 (stronger student?).

scenes.name: Asteroid
scenes.desc: STOP 4 answer. Kinetic impactor hits 2026-XJ: equal and opposite forces; 600 kg vs 3.5 × 10¹¹ kg. STOP 5.

scenes.name: Exit
scenes.desc: STOP 5 answer (a = F/m). Exit ticket: you push a wall; what pushes back? STOP 6.

scenes.name: Hold
scenes.desc: Hold on the exit ticket.

lessons.title: Free Body Diagrams Part 1
lessons.file: Day 15 - Free Body Diagrams Part 1 - In Class.dc.html
lessons.guide: Day 15 - Free Body Diagrams Part 1 - Teacher Guide.md

scenes.name: Title
scenes.desc: Day 15 · Building the tools: Free body diagrams, part 1. Target S5.

scenes.name: Intro
scenes.desc: Why FBDs: every force on one object, then F = ma. A book on a desk shrinks to a dot. STOP 1 (forces on the book?).

scenes.name: Rules
scenes.desc: Answer: F_g down, F_N up, equal lengths. The six rules appear one by one; rule 6 crosses out the book’s push on the desk. STOP 2 (box pushed at constant speed).

scenes.name: Box
scenes.desc: Answer: four arrows; push = friction, gravity = normal; net force 0. STOP 3 (ball at the peak).

scenes.name: Peak
scenes.desc: Answer: only gravity, even at v = 0. Common errors: momentum and inertia are not forces. STOP 4 (car on a curve).

scenes.name: Curve
scenes.desc: Answer: top view, friction toward the centre; FBD with F_g, F_N, sideways friction. Changing direction means accelerating.

scenes.name: Asteroid
scenes.desc: FBD of 2026-XJ: big Sun gravity arrow, small Earth arrow, others negligible, no friction or normal. STOP 5 (what does an impactor add?).

scenes.name: Exit
scenes.desc: STOP 5 answer: applied force along the impact. Exit ticket: box pulled by a rope with friction. STOP 6.

scenes.name: Hold
scenes.desc: Hold on the exit ticket.

lessons.title: Free Body Diagrams Part 2 - Net Force
lessons.file: Day 16 - Free Body Diagrams Part 2 - Net Force - In Class.dc.html
lessons.guide: Day 16 - Free Body Diagrams Part 2 - Net Force - Teacher Guide.md

scenes.name: Title
scenes.desc: Day 16 · Building the tools: Free body diagrams part 2, net force. Target R9.

scenes.name: Recap
scenes.desc: Net force is the vector sum. FBD of a 5 kg box: 30 N pull, 10 N friction. STOP 1.

scenes.name: OneD
scenes.desc: Answer: pick + direction, F_net = 30 − 10 = 20 N, a = 4 m/s². Then the floor tilts into a ramp. STOP 2 (which part of gravity pulls down the slope?).

scenes.name: Incline
scenes.desc: Answer: tilted axes; gravity splits into mg sin θ down the slope and mg cos θ into it; θ marked between F_g and the perpendicular.

scenes.name: Split
scenes.desc: Worked example: 2 kg, 30°, 4.0 N friction → 9.8 N down, F_N = 17.0 N, F_net = 5.8 N, a = 2.9 m/s². STOP 3 (frictionless 20°).

scenes.name: Space
scenes.desc: STOP 3 answer ≈ 3.4 m/s². 2026-XJ’s FBD is only gravity; a spacecraft orbiting Earth has gravity plus thrust. STOP 4.

scenes.name: Exit
scenes.desc: STOP 4 answer. Exit ticket: 10 kg box, 50 N push, 15 N friction. STOP 5.

scenes.name: Hold
scenes.desc: Hold on the exit ticket.

lessons.title: Friction
lessons.file: Day 17 - Friction - In Class.dc.html
lessons.guide: Day 17 - Friction - Teacher Guide.md

scenes.name: Title
scenes.desc: Day 17 · Building the tools: Friction, the force that resists motion. Target R10.

scenes.name: Hook
scenes.desc: A heavy crate strains, then slides; pushing gets easier. STOP 1 (why?).

scenes.name: Types
scenes.desc: Answer: static vs kinetic. Friction vs push graph rises to max static, drops to kinetic. f_s ≤ μ_s N, f_k = μ_k N; μ_s > μ_k. STOP 2 (10 kg box).

scenes.name: Lab
scenes.desc: STOP 2 answer: 49 N to start, 29.4 N to keep going. Investigation 1.5: pull at constant velocity, sensor reading = friction; surfaces cycle. STOP 3 (lab).

scenes.name: Data
scenes.desc: Example data: wax paper 0.15, paper 0.30, sandpaper 0.50; double mass doubles f and N; double speed, same f. STOP 4.

scenes.name: Space
scenes.desc: STOP 4 answer: μ unchanged. A puck on frictionless ice slides forever; 2026-XJ never slows by itself; a tiny push adds up. Gravity tractor preview.

scenes.name: Exit
scenes.desc: Exit ticket: easier because… / harder because…. STOP 5.

scenes.name: Hold
scenes.desc: Hold on the exit ticket.

lessons.title: Equilibrium
lessons.file: Day 18 - Equilibrium - In Class.dc.html
lessons.guide: Day 18 - Equilibrium - Teacher Guide.md

scenes.name: Title
scenes.desc: Day 18 · Building the tools: Equilibrium, when forces balance. Target R11.

scenes.name: Recap
